newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault H1 result seen close to zero.
newsitem.headline: Renault H1 result seen close to zero.

text.p: French carmaker Renault SA is expected to report half-year results on Tuesday evening ranging from a net attributable loss of 300 million francs to a net attributable profit of the same size, analysts say.
Some analysts said the spectrum may be wider, ranging from a 400 million franc loss to a 400 million franc profit.
"What's a few million francs for a company this size? Basically you're looking at a result of zero," said one analyst.
Renault, which reported a net attributable profit of 1.76 billion francs for the first half of 1995, is scheduled to report 1996 half-year results on Tuesday after 1500 GMT.
No industry consensus forecast is available as half-year earnings estimates are not compiled for French companies.
Analysts say the anticipated earnings drop is due to weakness in the European and French car markets and a fierce price war among manufacturers that has eroded profit margins.
Renault, the smallest of Europe's Big Six carmakers, has been especially hard hit, losing market share in Europe and in its domestic market.
The company has not given a half-year earnings forecast.
Renault's car division rolled into the red during the second half of 1995, and analysts estimate the division lost somewhere around one billion francs during the first half of 1996.
One analyst said he expected the truck operation to show a drop in profit and the financial division's results to be flat.

Analysts generally agreed Renault's performance picked up in the third quarter, helped by its new Megane models and a pickup in French car sales ahead of the September 30 deadline for a state rebate offer. But they said the fourth quarter would be tough following the expiry of the rebate scheme.

Full-year forecasts for the company have been sliding since April, when the consensus was for roughly flat full-year results compared with net attributable profit of 2.14 billion francs recorded by Renault for 1995.
Corporate research consultancy Jacques Chahine Finance said the median estimate was now for a 53 percent decline in full-year profit from 1995 levels.
Renault's shares have weakened ahead of the results and were down 0.51 percent at 117.10 francs on Monday at 1100 GMT.
